event: Engagement off Calais (morning to 19:00)
note: Gregorian date (Spain used the Gregorian calendar from 1582)

event: Pursuit ends; Armada retires
Three ships anchor off Streedagh
note: Wreck day minus 4 days at anchor (S016/S017); the voyage round Scotland is not timed in the text

event: Ships driven ashore and broken within an hour
note: Anchor date 21 Sep 1588 Gregorian (11 Sep Julian in English records); 'plainly visible from the battered ships'

event: Calm by about 21:00
note: Same evening as the wreck

event: About 200 horsemen ride past at about 01:00 without seeing him
note: Next calendar day (after midnight)

event: Walks inland at dawn to the burned monastery
note: 'At the dawn of day'

event: Back at the strand where the ships 'were wrecked three days before'; buries Don Diego
note: 'Three days before' read as 2 to 4 days after the wreck (inclusive or exclusive counting); the text does not account for the days in between

event: Stony road; leg wound; huts in the wood
note: Continuous narrative from the burial

event: Night at the huts of the Latin-speaker
note: 'That night I reached some huts'

event: Horse and boy at morning; 150 horsemen; stripped naked
note: 'In the morning they gave me a horse'

event: Reaches the lake with about 30 empty huts; night in the oat hut
note: 'I continued travelling little by little' then 'there I wished to pass the night'; same day or a few days later

event: Daybreak; buried in straw all day while reapers work outside
note: 'When... day broke'; oats being reaped

event: Nightfall; 'awaited the rising of the moon'; leave before day
note: Low-trust signal: tested in step 2

event: Huts of 'better people'; kept until fit; then O'Rourke's village
note: 'Did not permit me to depart till it appeared I should be well able'

event: 'Early next day' news of a Spanish ship; the twenty set out
Wandering; meets the clergyman; directed to a castle six leagues off
note: The ship sailed 'in two days'; Cuéllar arrived late and wandered

event: Taken to a blacksmith's hut; bellows for more than eight days
Clergyman returns; MacClancy sends for him 'the following day'
note: 'More than eight days' at the forge plus a day

event: Leaves MacClancy's castle two hours before dawn
note: 'Ten days after the Nativity in the year 1588' (Spanish year began at Christmas); gap = 'three months' at the castle (S098), read as 75-105 days

event: After 20 days' journey reaches the Girona wreck site
Hears of O'Cahan's vessels; reaches them two days late
note: 'Until one day I heard'

event: Hidden in huts on the mountain more than six weeks
note: 'More than a month and a half'

event: Flight from O'Cahan's village; night by a lake
note: English and O'Cahan march off; 'one afternoon'

event: Two days on the mountain with the cowherd boys; leaves very early
Reaches the bishop seven leagues off; six days with him
note: Seven leagues (about 30-40 km) for an injured man

event: Puts to sea at dawn; driven to Shetland; lands at daylight
Leaves Shetland after two days; arrives in Scotland after three
note: Overnight run to Shetland (1-2 days) + 2 + 3

event: Leaves Scotland after more than six months
note: 'Left for more than six months as naked as when we arrived'

event: Shipped past English ports to Dunkirk; wrecked at the bar; ashore in Flanders
note: Letter dated 4 Oct 1589 says 'arrived twelve days ago'

event: Letter written at Antwerp
